subject: [hw] R1 finding F3 (V15, MEDIUM): 16-bit parallel add/sub set only one GE bit per halfword
body:
File: gpu/hwcodec/emu/n2a32_t32_dp.c:585-588 and :618 (parallel_op).

For the halfword variants the Arm ARM gives each lane a TWO-bit GE field: GE[1:0] for the low halfword, GE[3:2] for the high (both bits 11 when the condition holds, 00 otherwise); only the byte variants use one GE bit per lane. parallel_op sets `ge |= cond << lane` for every lane and then masks with `lanes == 4 ? 0xF : 0x3`, so a halfword lane can only ever set GE[lane], and GE[3:2] is always 0.

Repro (my spot test, review/r1/spot/spot.c, encoding from llvm-mc):
  sadd16 r0, r1, r2 = FA91F002; r1=0x0001ffff, r2=0x00010001
  low: 0xffff+1 = 0x10000 (exact signed 65536 >= 0) -> GE[1:0]=11
  high: 1+1 = 2 (>= 0) -> GE[3:2]=11
  current: r0=0x00020000 ge=0x3; expected ge=0xF.
  Same for sasx/ssax/ssub16 and the U/UQ/UH variants (uadd16 with both lanes carrying -> 0xF).

Note the package test mirrors the bug: emu/test_v15/t_dp.c:909-931 expects ge 0x1/0x3/0x2 for the 16-bit cases (e.g. "sadd16 #2" wants 0x3). Those expectations were derived from the same one-bit-per-lane reading, so the suite cannot see it. The A32 V11 implementation gets this right (sets both bits), which is a useful cross-check.

Fix sketch:
  unsigned gbit = (lanes == 4) ? lane : 2u * lane;
  unsigned gwidth = (lanes == 4) ? 1u : 2u;
  if (cond) ge |= ((1u << gwidth) - 1u) << gbit;
  ...
  c->ge = (uint8_t)(ge & 0xF);
(cond = r >= 0 for signed; for unsigned add r > lane_max, for unsigned sub r >= 0).

Severity medium: wrong architectural state after a halfword parallel op; SEL and any code testing GE afterwards would differ. The vendor census does not list sadd16/ssub16, so it is unlikely to bite the hot path, but it is a real deviation and the test needs independent expectations. My spot run: 179/183; the failures are F1 (2), F2, and this one.
